semantics: Declared-Delta Registry (ADR 0021 decision 9) — the Translation Ledger repurposed: dispositions classify host-native deltas ABOVE the Contract Floor rather than translation loss. Every divergence carries exactly one classification (mapped | approximated | degraded | unsupported) plus a rationale; an undeclared divergence is a conformance failure (decision 6). Consumed by src/core/semantic-core.ts validateDeclaredDeltas and the per-host Conformance Suites. Plan 026 extended coverage from claude-only to antigravity and cline (docs/host-primitive-matrix.md is the human-readable view of this file).

entries.rationale: Authoring metadata for the canonical store; no Claude field needed.
Canonical role discriminator; Claude distinguishes roles by file location.
Canonical masthead flag; Claude decides main-thread status at launch (--agent).
Canonical masthead flag; every file under .claude/agents/ is a subagent.
Claude loads CLAUDE.md and project memory unless omitClaudeMd is set (flag-gated).
Antigravity shell policy has no Claude frontmatter equivalent; Bash permissions cover it.

Antigravity hook schema (PreInvocation/PostInvocation matchers) differs from Claude hook events; canonical prose hooks are not translated and stay advisory. The one enforced hook is the managed PreToolUse guard every role carries (Plan 022 H5).
Agent-referenced rules project into the lean .claude/rules/ lane.
Reasoning effort passes through to the Claude effort field.
Delegation maps to the Claude Agent tool (allowlist on coordinators).
Maps to the Claude SendMessage tool; cross-session reach differs from Antigravity messaging.

Maps to the Claude task tools (TaskCreate/TaskUpdate), but the live tools reference says they are "provided by default only on the models listed under Task tool availability, and on other models when you opt in" — so the grant can resolve to nothing depending on the model.
Maps to Cron tools, but Antigravity reactive liveness timers are event-driven rather than cron-scheduled.
Claude agents are pre-defined: runtime subagent definition is unavailable, so the prompt delegates via the Agent tool.
Claude manages subagent lifecycle itself; the roster is static and the prompt delegates via the Agent tool.
Claude exposes AskUserQuestion only in the main conversation (excluded from subagents by default).
Claude Code exposes no image-generation tool; asset creation must happen outside the agent run.
Claude subagents discover project skills and can invoke them; the canonical preload list is not injected to avoid paying its token cost on every spawn.
Claude supports per-subagent mcpServers, but the canonical descriptor dialect differs; MCP wiring stays host-configured via the MCP location registry (translation deferred).
Claude Code workflows are JavaScript orchestration scripts, unrelated to this repo's canonical workflow-as-skill model (ADR 0016); Claude JS workflows are not a projection target.

Above-floor host-native affordance (ADR 0021 decision 5): specialist reports are delivered back to the spawning conversation by the runtime (SubagentHandback, v2.1.271+, auto mode) instead of the specialist publishing them itself.

Above-floor host-native affordance (ADR 0021 decision 5): Agent Teams (opt-in) adds direct peer messaging beyond the floor's hand-back-only contract; the floor contract remains the default and the Teams path is never load-bearing.
Authoring metadata for the canonical store; Antigravity is the field's native home.
Canonical role discriminator; Antigravity's own department/role schema.
Native masthead flag; Antigravity reads it directly to decide main-thread status.
Native masthead flag; Antigravity reads it directly.
Native flag Antigravity honors as authored.
Native Antigravity shell-execution policy field; the canonical vocabulary is this field's origin.
Native `.agents/hooks.json` (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PreInvocation/PostInvocation/Stop) is the field's origin schema; canonical prose hooks pass through as authored.

Native rules with glob scoping; Antigravity additionally enforces a 24 KB per-rule-file budget and a ~20k-token aggregate for active rules, demoting oversize rules to pointers — a native constraint, not a translation loss.
Native reasoning-effort field.
Native subagent-invocation tool; the canonical token is this tool's own name.
Native cross-agent messaging tool; the canonical token is this tool's own name.
Native task-management tool; the canonical token is this tool's own name.
Native reactive liveness/scheduling tool; the canonical token is this tool's own name.
Native runtime subagent-definition tool; Antigravity roles can define subagents at runtime, unlike the pre-defined-roster hosts.
Native subagent-lifecycle-management tool.
Native interactive-question tool, available to every role including subagents.
Native image-generation tool; the canonical token is this tool's own name.
Antigravity is the only host that reads the canonical per-agent skills list directly; SKILL.md progressive disclosure (description always loaded, body on trigger) is native.
Native per-agent mcpServers descriptor; the canonical dialect is this field's own shape.

Antigravity workflows are markdown slash-command macros under `.agents/hooks.json`-adjacent `ide/workflows`, and are deprecated in favour of skills from 2026-11-01 (docs pull 2026-09-27); this repo already treats `workflow-*` skills as the canonical durable form (ADR 0016), so native Antigravity workflow macros are not authored going forward even though the runtime still accepts them today.
Authoring metadata for the canonical store; no Cline field needed.
Canonical role discriminator; Cline distinguishes roles by projection location (.cline/agents/*.yml vs bundle rules).
Canonical masthead flag; the coordinator role is the one whose rule stays always-active (.cline/rules/agents-united-<bundle>.md) while specialists become spawnable subagent_<name> tools.
Canonical masthead flag; every role projected to .cline/agents/*.yml is a Configured Agent, spawnable as subagent_<name> (ADR 0013).

Cline always loads active `.cline/rules/` content into every session; there is no per-agent opt-out equivalent to Claude's omitClaudeMd, so the canonical intent (customizations inherited) already holds unconditionally.
Cline has no per-agent frontmatter equivalent; command execution is governed workspace-wide by the CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS allow/deny/allowRedirects setting, not a role-level policy field.

Cline CLI has no end-user hook file; hooks exist only as an SDK/CLI plugin capability (code plugins under .cline/plugins/, not a YAML/markdown surface). The repo already strips `hooks:` from Cline projections (Plan 015 note); this entry records why.
Agent-referenced rules project into `.cline/rules/agents-united-<bundle>.md`; empirically confirmed to reach live Cline sessions as always-active instructions (ADR 0013, 2026-09-18 canary probe).
Cline configured agents have no reasoning-effort field; the closest lever is provider/model choice (providerId/modelId), which is a different axis and is not substituted for effort.
Delegation maps to the configured `subagent_<name>` tool Cline auto-generates per `.cline/agents/*.yml` file (ADR 0013).

Named peer-to-peer messaging exists only under the SDK's opt-in Agent Teams mode (`enableAgentTeams`/`--team-name`); the default Configured Agent path is spawn-and-return, closer to Claude's hand-back-only floor than to live messaging.
Cline's Focus Chain (`focusChainSettings`) tracks task/TODO state across a run, but it is a session-wide feature, not a tool a role invokes explicitly the way canonical manage_task is authored.

The Cline CLI/SDK ships real cron scheduling (`cline schedule create --cron "<expr>" --prompt ... --workspace ...`), a closer match to canonical schedule semantics than Claude's Cron-tool approximation.
Cline Configured Agents are pre-defined YAML files (like Claude's roster), not runtime-definable; the prompt delegates via the fixed `subagent_<name>` tool set instead of defining agents on the fly.
Cline manages Configured Agent lifecycle itself (spawn/run/return); the roster is static per `.cline/agents/*.yml` and the prompt delegates via the fixed tool set.

The Cline extension's own subagents (`use_subagents`, a separate read-only research surface) cannot ask the user anything; only the main session and the CLI's `--acp`/interactive modes can. No configured-agent tool corresponds to canonical ask_question.
Cline documents no image-generation tool for the main session or for Configured Agents; asset creation must happen outside the agent run.

Verified against cline/cline PR #9502 (merged 2026-02-24, shipped by 3.0.65, the currently published version): the Configured Agent `skills:` field is parsed (`AgentConfigLoader.parseSkills`), exposed via `SubagentBuilder.getConfiguredSkills()`, and consumed by `SubagentRunner.run()` to FILTER `getAvailableSkills()` down to the named subset before building `SystemPromptContext.skills` — the same metadata-only discovery objects the unfiltered path already uses (progressive disclosure: ~100 tokens/skill metadata always, full SKILL.md body only via the `use_skill` tool on trigger). It scopes which skills a subagent can discover, it does not preload full skill bodies. The canonical per-agent skills list therefore projects 1:1 into this field (Plan 026 Step 4).

`.cline/mcp.json` is documented on docs.cline.bot but absent from the installed Cline binary as of the last verification (ADR 0013 decision 7, scope exclusion); MCP wiring stays host-configured via the MCP location registry until Cline ships it.
Canonical `workflow-*` skills project into `.cline/workflows/<slug>.md` with a slugified frontmatter `name`, surfacing as a usable `/<slug>` slash command (ADR 0013).
